title: Profitability
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define profitability, explain why it matters to a business and its stakeholders, and keep profit apart from the cash that pays the bills.

blocks.heading: What profitability means
blocks.text: Profitability is the ability of a business to earn profit: revenue that is greater than the total costs of earning it, measured over a trading period and expressed in a currency such as Namibian dollars. A jeweller in Windhoek with revenue of N$200 000 and total costs of N$168 000 is profitable by N$32 000 for that period. A business whose costs equal its revenue breaks even; one whose costs exceed its revenue makes a loss, however busy it looks.

blocks.heading: Why profitability matters
blocks.text:
Profitability matters along a chain. Condition: a business earns profit when customers value its output above its full cost. Mechanism: the surplus rewards the owners for the risk they took, and it can fund expansion from the business's own resources instead of borrowing. Consequence: the business is more likely to survive hard trading periods, keep paying wages and suppliers, and attract further investment, because a steady profit signals that the business model works.

A family bakery in Lisbon that keeps its margins healthy can open a second shop from its own savings; one that trades at a loss year after year slowly eats its owners' funds and usually closes. The same chain runs through the stakeholders: workers keep a reliable employer and suppliers keep a customer worth trusting.

blocks.heading: Profit is not cash
blocks.text: Learners often treat profit and cash as one figure. They are not the same: profit is revenue less total costs over a period, while cash is the money actually available to pay bills on a given day. Because many sales are made on credit, the timing of receipts means a profitable business can still miss a payment date. The test: ask whether the statement is about the year's result, which is profit, or about money on hand today, which is cash.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Profitability is measured with the ratios of sub-topic 5.5.3 - gross profit margin, profit margin and return on capital employed. Topic 5.3 shows how profit is calculated in the income statement, 5.2 forecasts the cash that profitability alone may not deliver, and 1.4 links profit to the stakeholders who depend on it.
